about.paragraph1: I’ve been building for the web for the last three years, but my sense of what to build, and why, comes from the work I did before I wrote any code.
about.paragraph2: Before development, I worked in marketing, mostly on the analytical side. I spent less time on campaigns and more on data: market numbers, user behavior, and how people find and use a product online. SEO and SEM are applied psychology. You learn to hear what the data is shouting, and to notice what it only hints at.
about.paragraph3: I bring that background to every project. Clean code matters, but I judge my work by whether it solves the problem it was built for.
about.paragraph4: When I build with React or Next.js, state management and component structure are only part of the job. I also think about how the user got to the page, and about semantic markup that gives the content meaning to search engines and screen readers. I treat speed as a requirement, because I’ve seen in the data that half a second of delay is enough for people to leave.
about.paragraph5: Plenty of good developers build to the spec and stop there. They lose sight of the person using the product and the business goal that justifies building it. I’ve been on both sides. I used to be the one asking developers for data; now I build the systems that provide it.
about.paragraph6: Whether it’s an AI web app, a front end, a Django admin or a full-stack Node.js application, I start with the same question: what problem are we solving? The technology follows from the answer.
about.paragraph7: I don’t just build things right. I build the right things.
about.title1: Building for the human behind the screen

services.longDescription:
Off-the-shelf software makes your team work the way the software wants. I build web applications around how your company already operates: its processes and the numbers you check every morning. I work in short iterations, starting with an MVP, so you see something usable early and we adjust it based on how people use it.

Every project starts with a look at the process the software will support. A CRM gets built around your sales pipeline; a dashboard shows the metrics you track, not a generic set. Your team is more likely to use a tool that was built for them.

I use React, Next.js and PostgreSQL, deployed on AWS, and build with modular, reusable components so the application stays easy to maintain and extend as your business changes.
services.text: Tailored web applications: CRMs, dashboards, and internal tools built with modular components and agile delivery, fitting how your business works.
services.title: Custom business software

features: AI-powered web application development
LLM integration with OpenAI and open-source models
AI agents for multi-step business workflows
Chatbots for customer support and sales
Automated document processing and classification
Semantic search across your documents and data
Business-specific AI assistants (RAG)
Automated content generation and summarization
Predictive analytics and AI-powered dashboards
services.longDescription:
AI is useful when it solves a specific problem. I build web applications that connect Large Language Models (LLMs) to the workflows you already have, in ways you can measure, and I leave AI out where it doesn’t help.

That might be a support chatbot that answers routine questions so your team handles fewer tickets, a recommendation engine that suggests related products at checkout, or agents that sort and summarize incoming documents. Each one starts with the result you want and works back to the technology.

I work with the OpenAI API, open-source LLMs, vector databases for semantic search, and RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation), so the system answers from your own documents and data instead of general knowledge.
services.text: AI-powered web applications and LLM integration: chatbots, AI agents and assistants that take repetitive work off your team.
services.title: AI solution implementation

features: Business websites and high-conversion landing pages
Progressive Web Apps (PWA) with offline support
E-commerce platforms and product catalogs
Legacy website migration and modernization
Core Web Vitals and technical SEO optimization
Responsive design tested on phones, tablets and desktops
Authentication, payments, and customer portal systems
Fast MVP development to test ideas with real users
Deployment on AWS, set up to handle growing traffic
Reusable component libraries that keep the front end maintainable
services.longDescription:
Your website is often the first place a customer judges your business. I build sites and web applications that load fast, work on phones and desktops, and lead visitors toward the action you want, whether that’s booking a call or buying a product.

Performance is part of the build from the start. I optimize for Core Web Vitals as I go, which helps search rankings and makes the site quicker to use. I start with an MVP, get feedback early, and iterate based on how people use it.

Projects range from landing pages to full web applications with authentication, payments and dashboards, deployed on AWS. The code is built from modular components, so it stays maintainable after launch.
services.text: High-performance web applications: fast, responsive websites that work on any device and help turn visitors into customers.
services.title: Web development

features: Full technical SEO audit (crawlability, indexation, architecture)
Core Web Vitals and page speed optimization
Competitor analysis and keyword research
Content strategy and on-page optimization
Migration and redesign consulting with SEO preservation
Analytics setup and auditing (GA4, Search Console)
services.longDescription:
A good website still needs the right people to find it. I worked in digital marketing before I became a developer, so I look at SEO from both sides: what search engines and users respond to, and what has to change in the code to get there.

Every audit starts with data. I review your site’s technical architecture, Core Web Vitals, content structure and how you compare with competitors in search. Load time gets particular attention, because it affects both rankings and conversions. You get a prioritized action plan where each recommendation is tied to the business result it should move.

There are no tricks here. The work follows search engine guidelines, and I’ll tell you plainly what I think will make a difference and what won’t.
services.text: Technical SEO audits, speed optimization and search strategy to help your business get found and turn visits into customers.
services.title: SEO & technical consulting

intro: I work with small and mid-sized businesses, startups, and independent professionals who need software that does a specific job well: a website that brings in customers, an internal tool that removes manual work, or an AI feature that saves your team hours.

My background in marketing and analytics means every project starts with the business goal, not the technology. Before writing any code, I ask what success looks like, how you will measure it, and what your users need.
You work directly with me from the first call to launch. No account managers, no handoffs, and clear communication about scope, timelines, and trade-offs.
